newsitem.title: USA: Mail bomber gets death penalty in Alabama.
newsitem.headline: Mail bomber gets death penalty in Alabama.

text.p: Walter Leroy Moody Jr., who masterminded a wave of mail bombings across the South in 1989, Monday was sentenced to die in the electric chair for the murder of a federal judge killed in the bloody campaign.
The sentence was handed down against Moody, 61, of Rex, Ga., in Jefferson County Circuit Court for the death of 11th U.S. Circuit Judge Robert Vance of Alabama.
Vance died Dec. 16, 1989, when a package he was opening in his Mountain Brook home exploded. His wife, Helen Vance, was injured by the blast.
Two days later, a similar bomb killed black civil rights attorney Robert Robinson of Savannah, Ga.
Moody was convicted last year of sending four mail bombs from August through December 1989 to targets in Alabama, Georgia and Florida.
"It is the judgment of the court that the aggravated circumstances (of the case) far outweigh the mitigating circumstances," Judge William Rhea of Etowah County said as he imposed the sentence.
Meanwhile, Moody read a rambling statement in which he accused the judge of being part of a conspiracy against him.
Under Alabama law, the sentence qualifies for an automatic appeal.
